item.title: High court to hear case to decide where migrants can apply for asylum
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Supreme Court will hear oral arguments Tuesday in a case to determine if a migrant on Mexico’s side of a border crossing with the United States can legally apply for asylum when arriving at a U.S. port of entry. item.title: DMACC selects Lori Suddick as new president
item.description: Des Moines Area Community College has named Lori Suddick as its new president, with her arrival on campus tentatively set for June 15. item.title: Trump administration pushes to deport Kilmar Abrego Garcia to Liberia
item.description: WASHINGTON — The Trump administration is again trying to send the wrongly deported Kilmar Abrego Garcia to the west African nation of Liberia and urging a federal judge to dismiss a bar on his removal, according to legal documents filed over the weekend. item.title: ICE accused of maliciously staging a ‘sham’ hearing for Iowa detainee
item.description: The attorney for an immigration detainee held in the Polk County Jail says federal officials maliciously staged a “sham” court hearing orchestrated to keep his client behind bars. item.title: Airport chaos: TSA agents skip work, security lines expand, Trump sends in ICE to assist
item.description: Airport security workers missed work Monday at the highest rate since a partial government shutdown began in mid-February, the Department of Homeland Security said, and the Trump administration sent immigration officials to some airports in an attempt to keep lines moving. item.title: Iowa House sends ‘medical conscience’ bill to governor
item.description: The Iowa House approved a bill Monday allowing medical practitioners and health care organizations to refuse to participate in or pay for a health care service that goes against their conscience or religious beliefs. item.title: Iowa House passes restrictions on foreign involvement in health care, ballot issues
item.description: The Iowa House passed two measures Monday restricting foreign entities from health care ownership and ballot issue campaigns. item.title: US Senate confirms Mullin as next Homeland Security boss
item.description: WASHINGTON — The U.S. Senate voted Monday evening to confirm Markwayne Mullin to lead the Department of Homeland Security, which is responsible for carrying out President Donald Trump’s mass deportation agenda.
